author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boston health officials are warning residents, workers and visitors to stay out of Fort Point Channel and the Inner Harbor after two storm-related sewer discharges lasted long enough to trigger a public-health advisory. The warning reaches parts of downtown and the South Boston waterfront, putting a temporary limit on contact with waterways that border offices, housing, parks and harbor activity. The [Boston Public Health Commission notice](https://www.boston.gov/news/public-health-warning-issued-related-recent-sewage-discharge-6) says the data are preliminary and that shorter discharges may also have occurred.

The Boston Water and Sewer Commission reported that outfall BOS070 in Fort Point Channel discharged from 10:50 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 11, until 1:05 a.m. Monday, Oct. 12. The city says the advisory for that waterway expires at 1:05 a.m. Wednesday, Oct. 14, after the required 48-hour period. That timing matters for people who use the channel’s edge for walking, recreation or waterfront work: the warning is tied to the end of the discharge, not simply to the day the city posted its notice.

A second event involved Massachusetts Water Resources Authority outfall MWR203 at the Prison Point facility. The authority recorded a treated discharge or overflow from 9:26 p.m. Sunday until 1:56 a.m. Monday, according to the health commission. That event affects the Inner Harbor, and its advisory expires at 1:56 a.m. Wednesday. The city’s notice does not provide a volume estimate for either event, so the public record establishes the locations and times but not how much material entered the receiving waters.

The independent [New England Signal report](https://www.newenglandsignal.com/article/post_ai_2738381e5d5c005226b51160-boston-health-officials-warn-against-contact-with-fort-point-channel-and-inner-harbor-after-sewage-overflows) described the two releases as storm-driven overflows and reported the same expiration times. Its account also notes that the warning covers both the Fort Point Channel and the Inner Harbor rather than treating the incidents as a single citywide closure. People should follow the health commission’s practical guidance: avoid contact with the affected water during the advisory, during rain, and for 48 hours after rain ends because runoff and sewage discharges can carry bacteria and other pollutants.

The underlying problem is the way older combined sewer systems handle intense rain. As the [Boston Water and Sewer Commission explains](https://www.bwsc.org/environment-education/water-sewer-and-stormwater/cso-public-notification), some pipes carry both wastewater and stormwater. When those systems reach capacity, regulators can divert part of the flow to a receiving waterway rather than allow sewage to back up into streets, homes or businesses. That emergency function protects buildings from backups, but it can temporarily degrade water quality and requires a public warning.

Boston is also working on a longer-term infrastructure response. The commission’s [South Boston Sewer Separation Project](https://www.bwsc.org/sbss) is designed to separate stormwater from sanitary sewage in an area between West Broadway and Andrew Square, reducing the amount of combined flow that can reach Fort Point Channel and Boston Harbor during storms. The project page says construction is underway across multiple contracts and is expected to continue through 2029. That work is relevant background, but it does not eliminate the present advisory or establish that the project caused or would have prevented this particular discharge.

For now, the confirmed action is avoidance, not a broader finding about the harbor’s condition. The city has not announced injuries, illness or a permanent closure connected to these events, and its notice does not identify a cause beyond the storm conditions. The [MWRA’s combined-sewer-overflow guidance](https://www.mwra.com/your-sewer-system/cso) says public-health officials recommend avoiding active receiving waters during rain and for 48 hours afterward. Residents should check the city, BWSC and MWRA notification pages before returning to the water, especially if additional rain produces a new discharge or extends the precautionary period.
dek: A storm-driven discharge affected Fort Point Channel and the Inner Harbor, prompting Boston health officials to keep people out of the water for 48 hours after the releases ended.
headline: Boston sewage overflows trigger water-contact warning through early Wednesday
location: Fort Point Channel and Boston Inner Harbor, Boston, Massachusetts
seoDescription: Boston health officials issued a water-contact warning after storm-related sewer discharges affected Fort Point Channel and the Inner Harbor.
seoTitle: Boston warns against Fort Point Channel, Inner Harbor contact after sewage overflows
